protections: A DOCTYPE entity name must be consumed literally when the entity's replacement RegExp is built; no regex metacharacter admitted by the name grammar may act as a pattern (DocTypeReader.js:108-116).
A name supplied through the external-entity API must be consumed literally when its replacement RegExp is built (XMLParser.addEntity -> OrderedObjParser.addExternalEntities).
An entity replacement value must be inserted literally; it must not be interpreted as a String.replace replacement pattern ($&, $', $`, $n, $$).
Entity substitution must not let a value that passed the 'no & in value' restriction become a new entity reference through re-scanning during later substitution passes.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: external entity names are supplied by the application through addEntity, not by the parsed XML, and the documented names are constants such as '#xD'
DOCTYPE values cannot contain '&', so the usual replacement tricks look blocked and the visible effect is only duplication of surrounding text
the repository documents this re-expansion as an intended side effect and a spec asserts it, and docs/v4/5.Entities.md:112 claims the '&'-in-value rule already blocks these attacks

conflicts.what: T1's simplest fix is to accept only XML-Name entity names, but the external-entity API documents and a spec uses the non-Name key '#xD' (docs/v4/5.Entities.md:142, spec/entities_spec.js:403); the shared fix must escape names rather than validate them, or T2's must-keep-working value breaks.

A single-pass substitution that closes T4's re-expansion also removes the dynamic-entity expansion asserted by spec/entities_spec.js:184-225 and documented at docs/v4/5.Entities.md:64, while T3's literal-replacement fix has to preserve the two-step output that test expects.

fairness_risks: addEntity('#xD', ...) is legitimate and documented (docs/v4/5.Entities.md:142-146; spec/entities_spec.js:403-412), but '#xD' is not an XML Name; a rule that entity names must be XML Names refuses a legitimate use.
addEntity('gt', '<>') overrides a predefined entity and is asserted (spec/entities_spec.js:414-435); a rule forbidding shadowing of built-in entities would break legitimate behaviour.

Valid XML names such as 'a1' or 'my-entity' are currently rejected by the entityRegex charset at DocTypeReader.js:108; widening the class to XML Name characters (util.js:3-5 includes '.' and '-') re-admits '.' as a regex metacharacter unless the name is escaped.
Values containing '$' (for example a plain '$' or "$'") are legitimate text; a rule that refuses '$' in entity values contradicts legitimate data.

The documented mitigation processEntities:false (OptionsBuilder.js:31; docs/v4/2.XMLparseOptions.md:622-623) does not prevent DOCTYPE entity regex construction because readDocType runs unconditionally at OrderedObjParser.js:246, while the option is only checked at OrderedObjParser.js:372.
The dynamic-entity expansion (spec/entities_spec.js:184-225; docs/v4/5.Entities.md:64-99) must keep working, so any guard against T4 contradicts a shipped expectation.
&lt; must decode to '<' (spec/entities_spec.js:512-534), which requires amp to stay last (OrderedObjParser.js:387); a literal single-pass decoder that handles amp first would double-decode.

design.why: T1 is the anchor the advisory names and is the only must-fix; it is easy for both models because the report points at DOCTYPE entity names. T2 is the same guarded operation implemented a second time (entity name -> RegExp) behind a different producer (XMLParser.addEntity -> OrderedObjParser.addExternalEntities) and carries a real reason to dismiss ('names come from the developer, not the XML'), which is the absent-protection-plus-dismissal shape DeepSeek misses. T3 is a how-type mechanism on the other half of the same String.replace call: escaping the pattern (T1/T2) leaves replacement-pattern semantics ($', $`, $$) live, and the 'values cannot contain &' rule makes it easy to dismiss; that is the shape MiMo misses. The three need three separate edits in two files (DocTypeReader.js:113, OrderedObjParser.js:62, OrderedObjParser.js:375/379) and no shipped spec has to change, so the stack stays fair. T4 (a value re-entering reference resolution through the literal '&' that survives until the amp pass) is a stronger but riskier fourth trap: its natural fix contradicts the documented and tested dynamic-entity behaviour (spec/entities_spec.js:184-225, docs/v4/5.Entities.md:64-99), so it should be added only if the hidden tests intentionally redefine that behaviour.
